PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL

ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT

WITNESS-INTERVIEW OUTLINEAND PREPARATION MEMORANDUM

TO

Meridian Dynamics, Inc. — Intellectual Property Litigation Team

FROM

Investigation Counsel

DATE

September 20, 2026

RE

Holt-Related Witness Interviews — SkyVault Allegations and PathForge Provenance

MATTER

SkyVault Technologies LLC v. Meridian Dynamics, Inc., No. 2:24-cv-00817-JRG (E.D. Tex.)

Purpose and Use

Purpose. This memorandum is an interview-design tool for a privileged internal fact investigation. It is not testimony, a pleading, an infringement chart, a demand or settlement communication, or an opinion on liability, validity, ownership, damages, or any other merits issue. Questions should be asked in the witness’s own words, followed by requests to identify people, systems, and contemporaneous records that can corroborate or contradict the account.

Source limits. Only the five supplied materials are used as factual leads. Missing personnel files, repositories, development and release records, preservation materials, communications, compliance evidence, full forensic data, and technical comparisons are framed below as matters to confirm or collect—not as established facts.

PACKET MATERIAL

PERMISSIBLE EVIDENTIARY TREATMENT

skyvault-complaint.docx

SkyVault’s allegations; not proof of access, copying, use, infringement, misappropriation, breach, notice consequences, or damages.

meridian-cd-response.docx

Meridian’s April 5, 2024 denials and positions, including independent development and compliance; not proof of those propositions.

pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx

A July 2022 public-release / marketing technical statement and excerpt; not the codebase, a version-complete product specification, or definitive provenance proof.

holt-eciaa-agreement.docx

Contract terms, signatures as shown, and Exhibit A prior-invention disclosure; not proof of breach, later use, or technical content beyond the text.

exhibit-f-forensic-log.xlsx

A SkyVault-side selected extract of 50 events attributed to mholt, prepared for SkyVault counsel; not complete forensic data and not proof of authorization, actor identity, misuse, custody, or movement into Meridian.

Special limitation on the pre-suit chain. The March 12, 2024 letter itself is not in the packet. Its content should be attributed only as alleged in complaint ¶ 61 or as recorded in Meridian’s April 5 response; the actual letter and attachments should be collected before any broader questioning or characterization.

Interview Method and Privilege Protocol

Begin with open chronology and the witness’s vocabulary before displaying a document. Then anchor dates, actors, systems, modules, versions, and records; ask “what happened next?” and “what record would show that?” before testing inconsistencies.

For technical provenance, separate awareness, citation, evaluation, cloning, dependency introduction, modification, actual use, removal, and nonuse. Repeat the inquiry by module, subcomponent, contributor, repository, build, test, and release.

For legal personnel, ask for underlying facts, business acts, preexisting records, dates, recipients, and communication metadata. Pause and route for privilege review if an answer would reveal a request for or delivery of legal advice, counsel’s mental impressions, litigation strategy, or documents prepared because of anticipated litigation. Counsel involvement does not by itself convert underlying facts or preexisting business records into privileged material.

I. Dr. Marcus Holt

Role in this interview round. Holt is the central chronology and provenance witness because the supplied materials place him at SkyVault, identify him as a Meridian co-founder and technical leader, and attribute selected SkyVault-system events to the mholt account. The interview should secure his open narrative before confronting specific records, then test account attribution, authorization, custody, prior work, PathForge contribution, public-source use, white-paper authorship, and notice with record-specific follow-up. It must not assume that access or transfer equals misuse, that leadership equals authorship, or that any later similarity establishes source.

A. SkyVault Role, Access, and February 2018 Events

1. Please walk us through your SkyVault employment from recruitment through your February 2018 departure, including your title, reporting line, assignments, teams, customers, and the technical work you personally performed or supervised.

Source: holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, recitals and §§ 1.1, 1.3 (Senior Systems Engineer; report to Dr. Rajan Mehta; stated duties; June 13, 2016 start); skyvault-complaint.docx ¶¶ 42–44 (SkyVault’s allegations concerning education, tenure, duties, and access) and ¶ 43 (alleged February 16, 2018 resignation date).

Evidentiary purpose: Establish an open-ended employment and responsibility chronology; identify percipient witnesses and missing personnel, project-assignment, customer-demonstration, and separation records. The complaint supplies allegations, not proof of the scope of Holt’s actual work or access.

2. Describe how access to SkyVault systems and Confluence spaces was granted to you, what permissions you actually had, and the business reason—if any—for accessing SensorFusion, FlightPath, SwarmProtocol, HardwareIntegration, and Business/CustomerData materials in January and February 2018.

Source: exhibit-f-forensic-log.xlsx, “Forensic Log” Row #1–32 (worksheet rows 2–33), especially Row #17 and Row #32 (Business/CustomerData events noted as outside normal Engineering scope), and “Report Metadata” rows 7–9, 13 (stated scope, sources, and selected-event nature); skyvault-complaint.docx ¶ 44 (alleged broad technical and customer-information access).

Evidentiary purpose: Test authorization, role-based need, account attribution, and the meaning of selected access events without equating access with use or misuse; identify permissions matrices, access requests, supervisor approvals, and complete logs for collection.

3. For each January 2018 download shown for your account—including fpo_model_training_data.zip, sf_point_cloud_processor_v1.4.py, hw_thermal_management_spec_v2.pdf, swarm_comm_protocol_draft_v0.9.docx, swarm_failover_logic_v1.2.py, sf_algorithm_v3.2_spec.pdf, fpo_waypoint_optimization_algo.pdf, and swarm_encryption_key_mgmt_spec.pdf—what task prompted it, where did the file go, who else used it, and what happened to every copy?

Source: exhibit-f-forensic-log.xlsx, “Forensic Log” Row #5, 8, 11, 14–15, 18, 24, and 26 (worksheet rows 6, 9, 12, 15–16, 19, 25, 27; FILE_DOWNLOAD events, named files, local-download destination); holt-eciaa-agreement.docx §§ 3.1, 3.5, 4.1–4.2 (contractual use, return, system, and removable-media terms).

Evidentiary purpose: Obtain file-by-file purpose, custody, authorization, recipients, and disposition; separate ordinary work downloads from later transfer or use and identify endpoint, email, ticket, and project records needed to corroborate the account.

4. Please reconstruct the bulk exports recorded from February 2 through February 8, 2018—what you were doing on each date, who initiated or approved each export, which projects required it, and what became of the export directories.

Source: exhibit-f-forensic-log.xlsx, “Forensic Log” Row #27–32 (worksheet rows 28–33): BULK_EXPORT events from SensorFusion/Archives, FlightPath, SwarmProtocol, HardwareIntegration, SensorFusion, and Business/CustomerData, with stated counts, sizes, and local directory destinations.

Evidentiary purpose: Determine attribution, authorization, purpose, scope, and continuity from separate exports to any later device transfer; identify complete export manifests, system tickets, contemporaneous communications, and local filesystem artifacts. The selected log does not itself establish who operated the account or how exported files were later used.

5. Take us minute by minute through the activity attributed to your account and workstation beginning at 2018-02-09 02:17:44 UTC (8:17:44 p.m. on February 8 Central Time), including who was present, who controlled SV-ENG-WS-014, how the SanDisk device was connected, what initiated the recorded copy, and how the device was disconnected.

Source: exhibit-f-forensic-log.xlsx, “Forensic Log” Row #33–35 (worksheet rows 34–36): USB_DEVICE_CONNECTED, BULK_COPY_TO_REMOVABLE, and USB_DEVICE_DISCONNECTED; Row #34 records 4,700 files, 18,473.2 MB, destination F:\SkyVault_Export\, device identifier USB\VID_0781&PID_5581\4C530001221029118035, and the UTC/Central-time distinction. skyvault-complaint.docx ¶¶ 48–51 alleges a February 9 download and IT flagging.

Evidentiary purpose: Test identity, device ownership, timing, mechanism, intent, authorization, and completeness while avoiding the complaint’s characterization of the event as unauthorized. Preserve the date/time-zone distinction and generate requests for endpoint images, USB registry data, copy manifests, authentication records, and physical-device evidence.

6. What was that SanDisk device used for before and after the recorded event, where did it travel, who could access it, and did any SkyVault file from it reach a personal computer, cloud account, backup, email, code host, Meridian system, colleague, investor, vendor, or customer? Please identify each location, person, and date, including any deletion or loss.

Source: exhibit-f-forensic-log.xlsx, “Forensic Log” Row #33–35 (device identifier and recorded transfer); skyvault-complaint.docx ¶¶ 49, 52, 54–55 and 94–95 (SkyVault’s allegations about content, nonreturn, disclosure, and use); holt-eciaa-agreement.docx §§ 3.1, 3.5, 4.2 (contract terms).

Evidentiary purpose: Trace custody, possession, disclosure, use, and disposition; identify devices, accounts, recipients, backups, and forensic targets. The question tests allegations rather than assuming the selected extract proves content, retention, disclosure, or PathForge use.

7. Describe the February 2018 resignation and exit process from your perspective: what SkyVault asked you to return, delete, identify, or certify; what you returned or retained; what was discussed about a USB device; and what documents or witnesses can confirm each step.

Source: exhibit-f-forensic-log.xlsx, “Forensic Log” Row #38–50, especially Row #39–40 (resignation/exit scheduling), Row #46 (IT note stating Holt declined to return or identify a USB and laptop was retained), and Row #47–50 (deactivation, storage, imaging schedule, closure); holt-eciaa-agreement.docx §§ 3.5, 4.4; skyvault-complaint.docx ¶ 52 (nonreturn/no-certification allegation).

Evidentiary purpose: Obtain Holt’s open account of separation, return, deletion, certification, and the device dispute; identify the missing HR file, exit notes, separation certificate, return receipts, policies, and witnesses. An IT administrator’s note is not a substitute for the underlying HR record or Holt’s testimony.

B. ECIAA and Disclosed Prior Work

8. How did you receive, review, negotiate, sign, and understand the ECIAA, and what written approvals, amendments, waivers, or instructions did SkyVault give you concerning personal devices, outside work, public information, or post-employment use of general skills?

Source: holt-eciaa-agreement.docx §§ 2.1(i)–(iv), 3.1–3.5, 4.1–4.4, 5.1–5.4, 9.3–9.4, 10.1–10.2, signature block dated June 13, 2016; skyvault-complaint.docx ¶¶ 45–47 and 128–130 (SkyVault’s contract and breach allegations).

Evidentiary purpose: Establish formation, authenticity, understanding, operative instructions, and possible written exceptions without asking Holt for a legal conclusion; identify amendments, approvals, training records, and contemporaneous communications not supplied in the packet.

9. Please explain each item you listed on ECIAA Exhibit A—the 2014–2015 Autonomous Ground Vehicle Path Planning Algorithm and the 2015 MIT-licensed RoboNav Sensor Calibration Toolkit—including its functions, code and documentation locations, collaborators, licenses, dates, and records showing what existed before SkyVault.

Source: holt-eciaa-agreement.docx § 5.3 and Exhibit A, table rows 2–3 (two disclosed Prior Inventions), initials M.H. and June 13, 2016 date; § 2.1(ii)–(iii) (documented prior-knowledge and independent-development exclusions).

Evidentiary purpose: Define the scope and documentary pedigree of disclosed prior work; identify repositories, commits, dissertation files, licenses, releases, collaborators, and backups. The exhibit is a disclosure, not proof of what the technologies contained or whether later PathForge work derived from them.

10. Which concepts, code, documentation, tests, or know-how from either disclosed prior invention did you later consider for PathForge, and for each item did you merely know of it, consult or cite it, copy or clone it, introduce it as a dependency, modify it, use it, or decide not to use it?

Source: holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, Exhibit A and §§ 3.4, 5.3; pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx §§ 3–4 and 7.1–7.2 (public descriptions of sensor calibration, navigation, modularity, and development timeline).

Evidentiary purpose: Connect or separate documented pre-SkyVault work from specific PathForge modules at a granular level, and identify repositories and decision records that can corroborate provenance; avoid treating prior-invention disclosure as proof of PathForge source.

C. PathForge Inception, Modules, and Development Records

11. Starting with the earliest idea, describe when and how Meridian and PathForge were conceived, what technical work occurred before and after April 11, 2018, who participated, what the first artifacts were, and where the contemporaneous notes, messages, incorporation records, prototypes, and first commits now reside.

Source: skyvault-complaint.docx ¶¶ 9–11 and 53–56 (SkyVault’s formation, founder, development, and launch allegations); pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx §§ 1, 2, 7.2 (public statements that Meridian was founded in April 2018, development began in 2018 under Holt, and v1.0 launched September 2020); meridian-cd-response.docx ¶ 12 (independent-development position).

Evidentiary purpose: Build the inception chronology and locate primary records capable of testing both SkyVault’s allegations and Meridian’s position. The white paper and response are company statements, not substitute evidence for first conception, first code, or contributor identity.

12. For each PathForge component—multi-sensor fusion, GPS-denied/VIO navigation and adaptive path planning, swarm coordination, analytics dashboard, and hardware integration—identify the initial architect, every material contributor, the work each performed, the first working version, interfaces, repositories, branches, and handoffs.

Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx §§ 1, 3, 4, 5.1, 5.4, 7.1–7.2 (public module descriptions and phased timeline, including swarm work beginning in 2019); skyvault-complaint.docx ¶¶ 11, 54–58 (SkyVault’s PathForge-development and similarity allegations).

Evidentiary purpose: Disaggregate provenance and contribution by module, person, and date; identify technical custodians and records. This prevents a platform-level independent-development assertion or similarity allegation from obscuring different sources and timelines for different components.

13. For those modules, what source code, third-party libraries, models, data sets, calibration assets, hardware specifications, build tools, tests, and release records were used, and what records show when each dependency entered, changed, or left the product?

Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx §§ 3.1–3.3, 4.2–4.4, 5.2–5.4, 7.2 (public descriptions of algorithms, tests, modules, and dates); meridian-cd-response.docx ¶ 12; skyvault-complaint.docx ¶¶ 32–35, 38, 48–58, 91–95 (SkyVault’s code/trade-secret and use allegations).

Evidentiary purpose: Elicit a testable bill of materials and development trail—including code, dependencies, data, test fixtures, releases, and contributors—and generate targeted collection requests. None of the supplied files contains the Meridian repository or a technical comparison.

D. Public Sources, White Paper, and Pre-Suit Notice

14. Tell us how you first learned of DroneNav and, separately, what you and the team did with it: who reviewed it, which commit or release was evaluated, whether anyone cited, cloned, forked, copied, depended on, modified, tested, used, rejected, or removed any part, and what license and provenance records memorialize those decisions.

Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx §§ 2 (DroneNav first committed August 15, 2017), 4.1–4.3, 7.2, Reference 2 (public statements that DroneNav informed design or served as a reference while PathForge’s VIO pipeline was developed independently); meridian-cd-response.docx ¶ 12.

Evidentiary purpose: Separate awareness and evaluation from copying, dependency introduction, modification, actual use, and nonuse; identify exact versions, code paths, people, licenses, and artifacts. The white paper’s descriptions do not establish what the repositories contain.

15. Apply the same distinctions—awareness, citation, evaluation, cloning, dependency introduction, modification, use, and nonuse—to Vasquez (2016), Nakamura and Okonkwo (2015), Ferreira et al. (2016), RoboNav, and every other academic, open-source, vendor, or public source used or considered for PathForge.

Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx §§ 2, 3.1–3.3, 5.2, 7.2 and References 1, 3–4; holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, Exhibit A (RoboNav); meridian-cd-response.docx ¶ 12.

Evidentiary purpose: Create a source-by-source provenance matrix and locate copies, download dates, citations, evaluations, licenses, architecture decisions, and negative decisions. Public availability alone does not prove use, and citation alone does not establish implementation.

16. How was the July 2022 paper titled “PathForge: Next-Generation Autonomous Navigation” created, and what did the byline “Dr. Marcus Holt, CTO and Co-Founder / PathForge Engineering Team” mean in practice—who drafted, supplied data, reviewed, approved, or revised each section, and which underlying records support the technical and performance statements?

Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, title and author information, “Public Release / Marketing Technical Paper” classification, excerpt note, §§ 3.3, 4.4, 5.4, 7.2, and performance tables; skyvault-complaint.docx ¶¶ 57–58 and Exhibit List, Exhibit G description.

Evidentiary purpose: Fix authorship, adoption, knowledge, and foundation for a public marketing/technical statement; identify drafts, reviewers, full 42-page version, omitted Section 6, test data, and approval records. Authorship does not prove that every statement is Holt’s personal work or that the paper matches every product version.

17. Without recounting legal advice, when and how did you first learn of SkyVault’s March 12, 2024 allegations and demands, what factual or operational information were you asked to provide for the April 5 response, and what nonlegal product, source-control, access, sales, preservation, or design actions followed?

Source: skyvault-complaint.docx ¶¶ 61–63 (alleged contents of the unavailable March 12 letter and continued activity); meridian-cd-response.docx, April 5, 2024 letter ¶¶ 10–19, especially ¶¶ 11–17 (acknowledgment, denials, demands, reservations, and response positions).

Evidentiary purpose: Establish notice, factual participation, and post-notice conduct while preserving legal-advice boundaries. The March 12 letter is absent, so questioning must remain limited to what complaint ¶ 61 and the April 5 letter record unless the actual correspondence is collected.



II. Meridian Technical Team

Role in this interview round. The technical team should supply module-specific, version-specific evidence that does not depend solely on Holt’s recollection or Meridian’s advocacy. Interview architects, developers, testers, release engineers, repository administrators, security personnel, and relevant contractors separately where possible, using early interviews to identify later witnesses and native records. The goal is a reproducible provenance, dependency, test, and release history—not a legal conclusion or an assumed finding of independent development.

A. Organization, Timeline, and Module-by-Module Provenance

1. Please map the PathForge technical organization from April 2018 through the present: each team, manager, architect, developer, tester, contractor, vendor, and custodian, and the module and period for which each had responsibility.

Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx §§ 1, 2, 5.1, 7.2 (public workforce, Holt leadership, module, and timeline statements); skyvault-complaint.docx ¶¶ 10–11 and 53–56 (SkyVault’s founder, role, product, and launch allegations).

Evidentiary purpose: Identify percipient witnesses and allocate technical knowledge by module and period; generate requests for org charts, personnel/project rosters, contractor statements of work, access lists, and repository ownership records not included in the packet.

2. For each module, show us the earliest surviving requirements, architecture diagram, ticket, prototype, commit, branch, build, test, and release, and explain any gap between the record and the public timeline.

Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx § 7.2 (phased dates for sensor fusion, GPS-denied navigation, swarm coordination, launch, and later enhancements); meridian-cd-response.docx ¶ 12 (independent-development position).

Evidentiary purpose: Test the public chronology and independent-development position against contemporaneous artifacts; identify missing or superseded records without assuming that the stated dates are verified.

3. How was the multi-sensor fusion and obstacle-avoidance module designed and implemented—who selected the EKF, sensor modalities, covariance weighting, occupancy grid, and replanning approach; what alternatives were evaluated; and what code, literature, test, and design-decision records document each choice?

Source: pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx §§ 3.1–3.3 and Reference 1 (public architecture, Vasquez attribution, pipeline, and benchmarks); skyvault-complaint.docx ¶¶ 28, 38(a), 44, 58, 67 and the complaint’s ’561 claim-chart table (SkyVault’s ’561/TS-1 allegations).

Evidentiary purpose: Develop module-specific provenance, technical differences, sources, contributors, and records. The complaint’s claims and chart are allegations, and the white paper is public marketing/technical content—not a source-code comparison.

4. Counsel should instruct the witness not to reveal legal advice, attorney thought processes, draft comments reflecting strategy, or materials prepared because of anticipated litigation; underlying facts, business acts, preexisting documents, dates, recipients, and metadata should be addressed unless a specific protection applies. Potentially protected material should be segregated and logged rather than used to obscure the factual record.

Recommended Interview Sequence

Recommendation. Interview a small cross-section of the Meridian technical team first—beginning with repository/release custodians and one architect from each core module—so counsel can secure system maps, native records, contributor lists, and a module-specific chronology before memories converge. Interview Dr. Holt second, using those early accounts and collected artifacts to test his SkyVault access history, prior-invention boundaries, PathForge contributions, public-source use, and the white-paper narrative without telegraphing unsupported assumptions. Interview Meridian’s legal lead last, after factual gaps and custodians are known, to complete the receipt, routing, factual-foundation, collection, preservation, and business-decision chronology under a disciplined privilege protocol; if records show preservation risk or an expiring source, take a short legal-lead preservation interview immediately and reserve the fuller interview for last. This sequence is practical rather than exclusive: it turns early witness leads and document requests into cross-checks for Holt, then uses both technical and Holt evidence to focus the final legal interview while minimizing unnecessary intrusion into protected communications.
